1. Accused Munna Lal is facing trial in the present case on allegations that while driving a car in a drunken condition at a high-speed he hit it against deceased Sapna, a young girl of 10 years and caused her death.
Brief Facts 2.

On 25.12.2018 on receipt of DD No. 55A ASI Ompal Yadav (PW6) and Ct Satpal (PW4) reached at point of accident that is towards Jhuggi Camp, Railway washing line where the dead body of deceased Sapna was found.

C No. 209/2019 " State. vs. Munna Lal "
Accidental Duster car bearing registration DL-8CZ-2511 was also found at the spot.
3. PW2 Rajni Devi eye witness and mother of deceased Sapna met ASI Ompal and she gave her statement Ex.PW2/A to him.

Translation of statement reads as under:

" I along with my family lives at the above address and the way to reach these slums is a footpath through the Kikar bushes.
On which there are debris lying and it comes through potholes.
Today, on 25.12.2018 at around 03:40 PM, I was going from the railway washing line towards the slum with my 10 year old daughter, Sapna.

She was walking 10-15 steps ahead of me while playing, when suddenly a big brown color car bearing no. DL-8CZ-2511, which was being driven by Muna Lal Kabadi, a resident of the slum there, came into those pits driving very fast from the front.
I raised both my hands and asked him to drive slowly but he hit Sapna and Sapna was hit by both the front wheels.

Got stuck in the middle but Muna Lal Kabadi still did not stop the car and increased the speed of the car to run away from there and Sapna kept dragging with the car for 10-15 steps and then the car landed on a pile of debris on the side of the road and stopped after banging against kikar bushes.
After getting tied and being dragged along with the vehicle and being crushed between the pile of debris on the side and the vehicle, Sapna died there.

Seeing this, Muna Lal ran away from there,
which seemed from his gait that he had drunk a lot of alcohol.
I already know Munna Lal, who works as a scrap dealer near our slum.

Legal action should be taken against Muna"
C No. 209/2019 " State. vs. Munna Lal "
4.
Accused was taken for his medical examination and in the medical examination alcohol content in blood was found to be 231.6 mg/100ml.

On the basis of facts and circumstances, FIR was registered under section 304 IPC and further investigation was handed over to SI Ankur (PW12).
5.
Accused Munna was arrested by SI Ankur, he seized the driving license of accused and recorded disclosure statement of accused.
Post-mortem on the dead body of deceased was got conducted and vide report Ex.PW11/A, the cause of death was opined as cerebral damage as a result of blunt force impact.
6. Statement of Abhinav Arya (PW7) owner of the offending vehicle was recorded.
Statements of other relevant witnesses were recorded and accused was charge-sheeted to face a trial for the offences punishable under Section 304 IPC and 185 Motor Vehicle Act.
Charge 7.
On 02.05.2019 charge for offence punishable under section Section 304(II) IPC and 185 Motor Vehicle Act was framed against the accused.
Accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.

proved that the accused was under influence of alcohol and had every knowledge that his act can cause a death.

11. On the other hand it is argued on behalf of the defence that the accused was not driving the vehicle at the relevant time nor there is any evidence to substantiate this fact.

Accident:

The vehicle was being driven at a very high speed.

. (A court observation is made that witness has gestured that she had raised her both hands trying to caution the driver of the approaching vehicle that he should stop).
Munna Lal had not stopped his vehicle and hit his vehicle against my daughter Sapna and my daughter got trapped in the front wheel of the Car which was being driven by the accused.
The driver continued driving the vehicle and stopped after about 10-20 steps of hitting my daughter and the car stopped over a malwa lying on one side of the road alongside a Keekar tree.

After that the accused came out from the vehicle and tried to ran away.
The driver of the vehicle not moving properly and it appeared as if he was drunk.

Thereafter, a big crowd of people gathered.

PW2 after noticing the car driven by the accused at a high-speed, signaled accused to stop the car but accused did not and eventually car hit against the girl who was walking on the path thereby causing her death.

It is submitted that going by the deposition of the PW-2 it would be clear that no vehicle could be driven at high speed on that road.

20-30 km/hour could be a high due to narrow width of the path where vehicle is driven.

19. In present case indicator of the fact that car was driven at a high speed is the deposition of PW2 that despite the signal given by her to the accused who was driving the car to stop the car, accused did not slowdown the speed and despite the signal struck against her minor girl.

He deposed that accused took the keys of the car from him and after sometime he came to know that accused had killed a girl in an accident.
22. PW3 deposed in his cross examination that he called his employer soon after the accused snatched the keys from him and drove away the car.

testimony of PW7 (owner of the car) and testimony of PW3 Sunil Kumar from whom accused took the keys of the car and drove away the same proves beyond any doubt that the offending vehicle was being driven by the accused.
27. Section 185 Motor Vehicle Act:
Now, the next question is to be answered is whether accused was driving car under influence of alcohol?

28. In his statement recorded under section 313 CrPC accused does not dispute that he was taken to the hospital for his medical examination but stated that he was not physically examined by the Doctor.
In this regard prosecution examined PW10 Dr SK Kaakran who examined accused on the date of incident at about 6.55 PM.

Dr SK Kakraan deposed that on local examination of the accused,
it was found that accused was smelling alcohol positive and on examination of blood alcohol content, it was found to be 231.6 mg/100 ml.
MLC of accused is duly proved on record as Ex PW10/A
as such contention of accused that he was not medically examined is contrary to record.
Alcohol content in the blood stream of accused shows that he was intoxicated and was driving offending car under influence of alcohol.

Offence under Section 304 Part II IPC:
29.
Accused has been charged with the offence punishable under section 304 Part II IPC.

In Alister C No. 209/2019 " State. vs. Munna Lal "
Anthony Pareira v. State of Maharashtra, (2012) 2 SCC 648 Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
26.

entities.text: Anthony Pareira v. State of Maharashtra, (2012) 2 SCC 648
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Section 304 IPC provides for punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.

It reads as under:
"304.Punishment for culpable homicide not amounting to murder.--Whoever commits culpable homicide not amounting to murder, shall be punished with imprisonment for life, or imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years, and shall also be liable to fine, if the act by which the death is caused is done with the intention of causing death, or of causing such bodily injury as is likely to cause death;
or with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years,
or with fine, or with both, if the act is done with the knowledge that it is likely to State vs Munna Lal on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137021487/
7 cause death, but without any intention to cause death, or to cause such bodily injury as is likely to cause death."
27.
The above section is in two parts.

Although the section does not specify Part I and Part II but for the sake of convenience, the investigators, the prosecutors, the lawyers, the Judges and the authors refer to the first paragraph of the section as Part I while the second paragraph is referred to as Part II.
The constituent elements of Part I and Part II are different and, consequently, the difference in punishment.

28. For punishment under Section 304 Part I, the prosecution must prove the death of the person in question; that such death was caused by the act of the accused and that the accused intended by such act to cause death or cause such bodily injury as was likely to cause death.

As regards punishment for Section 304 Part II, the prosecution has to prove the death of the C No. 209/2019 "
State. vs. Munna Lal "
person in question; that such death was caused by the act of the accused and that he knew that such act of his was likely to cause death.
In order to find out that an offence is "culpable homicide not amounting to murder"--since Section 304 does not define this expression-- Sections 299 and 300 IPC have to be seen.

30. As stated in above authoritative judgment, to prove this offence, prosecution must prove that the death of the person in question; that such death was caused by the act of the accused and that he knew that such act of his was likely to cause death.
31. Post-mortem report Ex PW11/A of deceased Sapna prepared by PW11 Dr Munish Wadhawan proves that deceased died due to cerebral damage as a result of blunt force impact.
All the injuries were found ante-mortem.
Thus, prosecution proved that Sapna met an unfortunate accidental death.
32. As stated above, accident was caused by the car driven by accused under influence of alcohol.
The fact that accused was under influence of alcohol stands proved on record.
Testimony of PW3 Sunil shows that accused snatched the keys of the car from his hand and drove the vehicle despite a protest made by Sunil Kumar.
33. It is not the case here that accused was driving the car in any unknown territory.

It is in the deposition of eye witness Rajni that accused Munna Lal was the resident of C No. 209/2019 " State. vs. Munna Lal "
the locality where the accident happened.
Accused was very well aware of the narrow roads and the path on which he was driving.
Accused was also aware that the way leads to the cluster area, which is populated.
34. Moreover, testimony of PW2 Rajni shows that she signaled accused to stop the car but accused did not do so.

Accused even after striking against deceased Sapna kept driving the vehicle and State vs Munna Lal on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/137021487/
8
eventually the vehicle was stopped in the bushes.
Photographs Ex PW2/D-2 & D-4 of the car, shows that car is stationed in the bushes.
Photographs indicates that accused might have lost control over the car and rammed it in bushes.
Accused did not give any explanation in his statement recorded U/s 313 Cr.P.C. in this regard and rather he took a defence that he was not driving the car.
35. A young child came under the front wheels of the car.
This fact also stands proved by the mechanical inspection report Ex.PW9/A, which shows fresh damages on the front bumper.
True that young child was walking on the road but she was in the vision of her mother.
Accused was driving under influence of liquor on a narrow road leading to populated cluster area.

Accused being aware of the locality was bound to take extra care and caution rather he under the influence of liquor without caring for the signal given by mother of decesaed, hit a young child and crushed her under the front wheel of the car being driven by him.

C No. 209/2019 " State. vs. Munna Lal "
36.

Though the defence has argued that the statement Ex. C-1 of Rajni Devi (PW-2) indicates that she was not aware about the registration number of the offending vehicle and further the fact that she settled the MACT case despite objections raised by the accused that he was not driving the offending vehicle, but neither the statement Ex.C-1 indicates that complainant admitted that accused was not driving the offending vehicle nor the settlement in the MACT claim proves this fact.
37. There is a presumption that a man knows the natural and likely consequences of his acts.
Moreover, an act does not become involuntary act simply because its consequences were unforeseen.
The cases of negligence or of rashness or dangerous driving do not eliminate the act being voluntary.

38. In the present case, following facts emerge:
i) Accused forcefully took the car from PW3 Sunil and drove the car.
ii) Accused drove the car under influence of liquor.
iii) Despite a narrow road accused drove the vehicle with speed and despite signal given by Rajni accused did not stop the car.
iv) Accused could not control the car and crushed deceased under front wheel of car.

C No. 209/2019 " State. vs. Munna Lal "
v) Even after causing accident, accused did not stop the car.
vi) Eventually car was stopped after it banged against the bushes.
